data.narrative:
Corvex Systems is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $5M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (277810.KQ), including peers such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

The stage-progression method is applicable and provides the primary valuation anchor. Using the $5M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to next-stage produces an implied valuation of $12.5M. The peer-median approach could not be reliably applied due to insufficient narrow-set comparables; while 11 same-sector peers exist in the robotics and manufacturing universe, the filtered peer set (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier valuation) contained fewer than three datapoints, making sector-wide aggregation potentially misleading.

The triangulated valuation range is $11M to $14M, with a median of $12M. This range reflects the single applicable method and carries material uncertainty stemming from the thin comparable set at Seed stage in this sector. Key variables affecting any refinement include the timing and stage definition of the next funding round, competitive positioning within the identified peer cohort, and technology differentiation relative to Exotec, Locus Robotics, and other direct competitors. Additional revenue or product-stage data would strengthen conviction in this range.
